children.text:
开场 1：为了阻止梦境与清醒世界之间的融合，你决定以肉身强行闯入「幻梦境」——你那位新同伴伦道夫如此称呼这个维度——而不是在睡梦中前往彼处。「这种方式危险重重，但我认为它胜过另一种选择，」伦道夫声称。「如果我们睡着时前往那里，就可能像你的同伴一样被困住，再也无法醒来。」你表示同意：被困在另一侧，你什么也做不了，尤其是你还想帮助那些正在做梦的同伴。

「我们的第一步是找到一把钥匙。即便在幻梦境与清醒世界接壤的地方，人也不能就这么走过去。我曾经拥有一把通往梦境之门的钥匙，但多年前把它弄丢了，此后再也没能找到，」他哀叹道。

查看战役日志。

• 如果黑猫在你身边，前往〈开场 2〉。

• 否则，跳过，直接前往〈开场 3〉。

开场 2：黑猫栖在附近的公园长椅上，眯起细长的眼睛，轻蔑地瞪着伦道夫。「你把幻梦境的钥匙弄丢了？」

你与猫一样满腹怀疑。伦道夫叹了口气，摇了摇头。「让我解释一下，」他对你说。「那不是一把实体的钥匙，从来都不是。那把『钥匙』是惊叹、幻想与创造力——它们在我年轻时点燃了我的想象。而这些正是我们成年后不再珍视的东西。通往这类梦境的钥匙随年岁流逝而丢失，再自然不过。」

「真是愚不可及！」黑猫斥道。「把想象力抛在身后，可不叫『成熟』。你抛弃了自己身上最好的部分。现在的你，比我见过的任何一个孩子都更像一只嗷嗷叫的猫崽。」

「也许你说得对，」伦道夫沮丧地承认。「我强迫自己相信，尘世的俗务比那些幼稚的幻想更重要——镶金的尖塔、芬芳的丛林、暮色中的国度……而现在，我恐怕再也见不到这样的奇景了。」他转回身面向你，眼中满是悔恨。「更糟的是，我无法为你引路了。」

跳过，直接前往〈开场 4〉。

开场 3：你照例走了一遍流程：「你最后一次见到它是什么时候？」「你最后一次用它是在哪里？」诸如此类。

伦道夫叹了口气，摇了摇头。「你不明白。那不是一把实体的钥匙，从来都不是。那把钥匙是惊叹、幻想与创造力——它们在我年轻时点燃了我的想象。而这些正是我们成年后不再珍视的东西。通往这类梦境的钥匙随年岁流逝而丢失，再自然不过。」

前往〈开场 4〉。

开场 4：你问他，究竟是什么让他的心思从奇幻之物转向了更实际的考虑。他思索了片刻，反复掂量着各种可能。接着，他瞪大了眼睛，意识到了一件重要的事。「很多年前出过一件事。那是我最后一次牵扯进超自然的东西——我是说，在今天之前，」他解释道。「我在商人区那栋废弃老宅旁的墓地里，遇见了我的一个朋友——乔尔·曼顿。就是他们称作不可名状之物的那栋宅子。我不想相信那里真如传说所言闹鬼，可我仅仅是复述了那个传说，就招来了那东西的怒火。」你问起那东西，伦道夫闭上眼睛，一阵剧烈的战栗沿着脊背窜上来。「它无法被描述。我只知道我们勉强活了下来。乔尔受伤是我的错。从那天起，我就再也不愿深究超自然或迷信之事。不是因为我信，而是因为我害怕。这就是钥匙躲着我的原因吗？这就是我再也不能做梦的原因吗？」领悟如白昼般击中了他。「我知道我们该去哪儿了。我就是在那里丢了钥匙。那里一定能把它找回来！」他瞪大眼睛喊道。

伦道夫手忙脚乱地想要拦一辆出租车，你这才明白他打算去哪儿：去那栋无名之屋，去那个至今仍在他记忆中作祟、难以描述的怪物所在之处……
从以下遭遇组收集所有卡牌：万千骇形、地下世界生物、现实交融、刺骨严寒、食尸鬼、紧锁之门、鼠群。
将以下地点放入游戏：坟地、前廊、楼上的走廊、两张楼下的门道，以及两张楼上的门道（推荐的地点摆放见下一页）。
每名调查员从坟地开始游戏。
将以下卡牌放在一边，置于游戏外：阁楼地点、无名坟墓地点、全部 6 个神秘阶梯地点、全部 4 张无尽深入诡计，以及银钥匙剧情支援。
将剩余的遭遇卡洗混，组成遭遇牌库。
如果因为每名调查员都被击败而没有达成任何结局：前往〈结局 2〉。

结局 1：这里与维吉尔·格雷在故事中写到的神秘森林、迷人的中世纪村庄和壮丽全景截然不同。不，恰恰相反：这片寒冷荒凉的深渊正一点点吞噬你的希望，代之以空洞而无意义的恐惧。你问伦道夫，这里是不是通往你那几位昏迷同伴的路。你几乎希望自己走错了方向，好把这可怕的地方抛在身后。

「我不知道，」他答道，一边从楼梯旁的窗户向外张望。「我们已经越过了清醒世界，但这里是幻梦境的低层界域，被称为地下世界。那是个不宜久留的地方。我们见过的许多越界进入我们世界的生物，都来自这片区域。也许我们的钥匙早就知道，这里才是我们真正的目的地？」你的向导端详着你在那栋废弃宅子里找到的秘术钥匙，手指抚过它上面的阿拉伯式花纹，仿佛在回忆它的形状、重量与质地。他因失去之深而眼眶湿润。

你主动提出替他拿着钥匙，这把他从独自的思绪中拉了回来。「啊。对，也许这样最好，」他说着，把这件精致的器物交到你手上。对一件据伦道夫说并不真实的东西来说，它重得出奇。

带着伦道夫和银钥匙，你重新踏上向下的路。你的同伴也许在地下世界，也许不在，但如果那些入侵清醒世界的生物确实来自这里，那么也许你能在此找到答案。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「伦道夫安全下降到地下世界」。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「调查员持有银钥匙」。任意一名调查员可以选择将银钥匙（梦境之门的钥匙）加入自己的牌库。此卡不计入该调查员的牌库张数。

• 每名调查员获得经验，数值等于胜利区中每张卡牌的胜利 X 值。

• 你的肉身如今行走在沉睡的幻梦境之中。在战役余下的时间里，向混乱袋添加 1 个 [skull] 标记。

• 如果你以四章战役的形式进行梦网，前往〈剧本 3–B：无归之地〉。

• 如果你以互联的八章战役形式同时进行梦寻与梦网……

• ……且尚未进行〈剧本 2–A：寻觅卡达斯〉，前往该剧本。

• ……且已经进行过〈剧本 2–A：寻觅卡达斯〉，改为前往〈幕间 II：入梦者〉。

结局 2：你清醒时最后的感受，是一阵恶臭冰冷的疾风——那无名而庞大的畸形之物疯狂扭打着，把你掀翻在地。肺里的空气被抽走，你叫不出声。你拼命抓挠地面，那东西撕扯你的皮肤，践踏你的骨头。你不知怎地挣脱出来，从那东西周围苦涩摧折的旋风中逃开。你听见墙皮剥落的刮擦声，碎屑抽过你的头顶，一块松动的砖砸中你的肩膀。你不禁想，等这一切结束时，还会剩下一栋能让人颤抖的房子吗。

• 如果调查员「找回了一把奇怪的钥匙」，前往〈结局 3〉。否则，跳过，直接前往〈结局 4〉。

结局 3：在环绕你的冰冷气流漩涡中，你几乎听不见伦道夫的呼喊。尽管希望渺茫，你还是设法到了他身边，而那难以描述的怪物紧追不舍。伦道夫掰开你的手，抓过你在那栋无名宅子里找到的钥匙，紧紧攥住。他闭上眼睛，低声念了些什么，听不清。当那可憎的洪流撞上你们时，一切陷入黑暗。

你醒来时，躺在一处平坦的石台上，俯瞰着一道陡直、笔直、通往未知深处的阶梯。在你身后，阶梯向上盘旋，没入一座升向迷雾的石塔。向两个方向望去，整座洞窟都被灰色的磷光微微照亮。伦道夫把你拉了起来。「刚才真是好险，」他承认道。「我再也不想经历那样的旅程了。」你问这是哪里，他咬着嘴唇，望向荒凉萧瑟的景色。

「这里是幻梦境的低层界域，被称为地下世界。那是个不宜久留的地方。我们见过的许多越界进入我们世界的生物，都来自这片区域。也许我们的钥匙早就知道，这里才是我们真正的目的地。我想……我想它现在已经消失了，」你的向导解释道。

你震惊得说不出话。伦道夫见你这般反应，咬紧牙关，羞愧地别过脸去。「算了。反正我们也不再需要它了。走吧。」他简短的回答在石阶间回响。由伦道夫带路，你重新踏上向下的路。你的同伴也许在地下世界，也许不在，但如果那些入侵清醒世界的生物确实来自这里，那么也许你能在此找到答案。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「伦道夫安全下降到地下世界」。

• 每名调查员获得经验，数值等于胜利区中每张卡牌的胜利 X 值。

• 你的肉身如今行走在沉睡的幻梦境之中。在战役余下的时间里，向混乱袋添加 1 个 [skull] 标记。

• 如果你以四章战役的形式进行梦网，前往〈剧本 3–B：无归之地〉。

• 如果你以互联的八章战役形式同时进行梦寻与梦网……

• ……且尚未进行〈剧本 2–A：寻觅卡达斯〉，前往该剧本。

• ……且已经进行过〈剧本 2–A：寻觅卡达斯〉，改为前往〈幕间 II：入梦者〉。

结局 4：在瓦砾之中，你看见了它：冰冷气流与尘埃的漩涡里有什么在闪光，有什么在呼唤你，低语着你的名字。你几乎听不见伦道夫的喊叫，那难以描述的怪物正撞向他。尽管希望渺茫，你还是设法到了那片废墟——那里曾是无名之屋的阁楼。你现在明白了那道难以捉摸的微光是什么：一把明亮的银钥匙打磨过的反光。「用它！」伦道夫在痛苦的叫喊之间嘶声道。那可憎之物爬上他的身体。「趁你还能——」

那东西裹住伦道夫的身体，把他的叫声截断。你把钥匙紧紧攥在手中，看着万千骇形将伦道夫整个吞下，不禁战栗。你想到你那几位同伴，他们被困在远离家乡、危机四伏的梦境某处；钥匙的光芒随之变亮，将你吞没，就像那东西吞没伦道夫一样彻底。一切化作一片白。

你醒来时，躺在一处平坦的石台上，俯瞰着一道陡直、笔直、通往未知深处的阶梯。在你身后，阶梯向上盘旋，没入一座升向迷雾的石塔。向两个方向望去，整座洞窟都被灰色的磷光微微照亮。你寻找银钥匙，它却不见了踪影。也没有伦道夫·卡特的任何迹象。

你显然已不在清醒世界中。也许那把钥匙真如伦道夫所说，把你的肉身送进了幻梦境。但这里与维吉尔·格雷在故事中写到的神秘森林、迷人的中世纪村庄和壮丽全景截然不同。不，恰恰相反：这片寒冷荒凉的深渊正一点点吞噬你的希望，代之以空洞而无意义的恐惧。你再次望了望身后数不尽的台阶。看来你如今别无选择，只能继续前行，深入这片荒凉而危险的领域。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「伦道夫在下降到地下世界的途中遇难」。如果某名调查员的牌库中包含伦道夫·卡特（现世囚困）（《食梦者》第 79 号卡），在战役余下的时间里，把他从该牌库中移除。

• 每名调查员获得经验，数值等于胜利区中每张卡牌的胜利 X 值。

• 如果你以四章战役的形式进行梦网，前往〈剧本 3–B：无归之地〉。

• 如果你以互联的八章战役形式同时进行梦寻与梦网……

• ……且尚未进行〈剧本 2–A：寻觅卡达斯〉，前往该剧本。

• ……且已经进行过〈剧本 2–A：寻觅卡达斯〉，改为前往〈幕间 II：入梦者〉。

intro.title: Scenario II–B: A Thousand Shapes of Horror

children.text:
Intro 1: To stop the merging between the land of dreams and the waking world, you decide to force your way into the “Dreamlands”—as your new companion Randolph calls the dimension—in your physical body, instead of traveling there in your sleep. “While there are many dangers to this method of travel, I think it is better than the alternative,” Randolph claims. “If we venture there in our sleep, we may become trapped like your companions, unable to wake.” You agree: you can do little good trapped on the other side, especially if you aim to help your dreaming companions.

“Our first step is to find a key. Even in places where the Dreamlands borders the waking world, one cannot simply walk between them. I once possessed a key to the Gate of Dreams, but I lost it years ago and have been unable to find it since,” he laments.

Check Campaign Log.

• If the black cat is at your side, proceed to Intro 2.

• Otherwise, skip to Intro 3.

intro.title: Scenario II–B: A Thousand Shapes of Horror

children.text:
Intro 2: The black cat, perched on a nearby park bench, glares at Randolph with narrow, disdainful eyes. “You lost the key to the Dreamlands?”

You share in the cat’s skepticism. Randolph sighs and shakes his head. “Let me explain,” he says to you. “It is not a physical key. It never was. The ‘key’ was the sense of wonder, fantasy, and creativity that sparked my imagination when I was young. These are things we do not value in maturity. It is only natural the key to these kinds of dreams should be lost with age.”

“What foolishness!” the black cat scolds. “It is not ‘maturity’ to leave one’s imagination behind. You have abandoned the best part of you. You are more a mewling kitten now than any child I have ever met.”

“Perhaps you are right,” Randolph agrees, downcast. “I forced myself to believe that earthly concerns were more important than juvenile fantasies of gilded spires, perfumed jungles, and twilight realms...and now I fear I shall never see such wonders again.” He turns back toward you, his eyes full of regret. “And worse, I will be unable to guide you.”

Skip to Intro 4.

intro.title: Scenario II–B: A Thousand Shapes of Horror

children.text:
Intro 3: You go through the usual motions: “When was the last time you saw it?” “Where was the last time you used it?” and the like.

Randolph sighs and shakes his head. “You do not understand. It is not a physical key. It never was. The key was the sense of wonder, fantasy, and creativity that sparked my imagination when I was young. These are things we do not value in maturity. It is only natural the key to these kinds of dreams should be lost with age.”

Proceed to Intro 4.

intro.title: Scenario II–B: A Thousand Shapes of Horror

children.text:
Intro 4: You ask what might have turned Randolph’s mind away from the fantastical and toward more practical concerns. He thinks for a brief time, mulling over the possibilities. Then, his eyes go wide as he realizes something important. “There was an incident many years ago. It was the last time I was involved with something supernatural—that is, before today,” he explains. “I met a friend of mine—Joel Manton— in the graveyard next to the old abandoned house in the Merchant District. The one they call the Unnamable. I didn’t want to believe that it was truly haunted, as the stories told, but in merely repeating the legend, I drew the creature’s ire.”You ask of the creature, and Randolph closes his eyes as a violent shudder courses up his spine. “It cannot be described. All I know is that we barely survived. It was my fault Joel was hurt. From that day forth, I have had no desire to delve into the supernatural or the superstitious. Not because I did not believe, but because I was frightened. Is that why the key eludes me? Is that why I can no longer dream?” The realization hits him, clear as day. “I know where we have to go. That is where I lost the key. That must be where it can be regained!” he exclaims, wide-eyed.

As Randolph frantically tries to hail a taxicab, you realize where he means to go: to the house without a name, where the indescribable creature that still haunts his memory resides...
Gather all cards from the following encounter sets: A Thousand Shapes of Horror, Creatures of the Underworld, Merging Realities, Chilling Cold, Ghouls, Locked Doors, and Rats.
Put the following locations into play: Burial Ground, Front Porch, Upstairs Hallway, both Downstairs Doorways, and both Upstairs Doorways (see suggested location placement on next page).
Each investigator begins play at the Burial Ground.
Set the following cards aside, out of play: the Attic location, the Unmarked Tomb location, all 6 Mysterious Stairs locations, all 4 Endless Descent treacheries, and The Silver Key story asset.
Shuffle the remainder of the encounter cards to build the encounter deck.
If no resolution was reached because each investigator was defeated: Proceed to Resolution 2.

Resolution 1: This place is nothing like the mystical forests, charming medieval villages, and majestic panoramas of which Virgil Gray wrote in his stories. No, far from it: this cold, bleak gulf eats away your hope and replaces it with a feeling of empty, meaningless dread. You ask Randolph if this is the way to your comatose companions. You almost hope that you are traveling in the wrong direction, so you can leave this awful place behind.

“I do not know,” he replies, peering out one of the windows along the stairway. “We have traveled beyond the waking world, but this is the lower plane of the Dreamlands, known as the Underworld. It is an inhospitable place. Many of the creatures we have seen crossing over into our world come from this region. Perhaps our key knew this was our true destination?” Your guide examines the arcane key you found in the abandoned house, running his fingers over its arabesques as though recalling its shape, its weight, its texture. His eyes water with the depth of his loss.

You offer to hold the key for him, which yanks him from his private thoughts. “Ah. Yes, perhaps that would be best,” he says, handing the delicate artifact to you. It is surprisingly heavy for something that, according to Randolph, is not real.

With Randolph and the Silver Key in tow, you continue your descent anew. The Underworld may or may not be where your companions are, but if the creatures invading the world of the waking are indeed from this place, then perhaps here you can find answers.

• In your Campaign Log, record Randolph survived the descent.

• In your Campaign Log, record the investigators possess the Silver Key. Any one investigator may choose to add The Silver Key (Key to the Gate of Dreams) to their deck. This card does not count toward that investigator’s deck size.

• Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display.

• Your body now walks within the slumbering Dreamlands. Add 1 [skull] token to the chaos bag, for the remainder of the campaign.

• If you are playing The Web of Dreams as a four-part campaign, proceed to Scenario 3–B: Point of No Return.

• If you are playing The Dream-Quest and The Web of Dreams as an interconnected eight-part campaign…
• …and you have not yet played Scenario 2–A: The Search for Kadath, proceed to that scenario.

• …and you have already played Scenario 2–A: The Search for Kadath, proceed instead to Interlude II: The Oneironauts.

Resolution 2: Your last waking sensation is the rush of noxious, frigid air as you are knocked to the ground by the thrashing, monolithic abomination with no name. The wind is pulled out of your lungs. You cannot scream. You grasp desperately at the ground as the creature tears at your skin and tramples your bones. Somehow you wrench yourself free, escaping through the vortex of bitter, withering wind surrounding the creature. You hear the scrape of peeling plaster. Debris whips past your head. A loose brick hits your shoulder. You wonder if there will even be a building left to tremble at when this is all over.

• If the investigators “recovered a strange key,” proceed to Resolution 3. Otherwise, skip to Resolution 4.

Resolution 3: You barely hear Randolph shouting to you over the maelstrom of ice-cold air that surrounds you. Despite all odds, you somehow reach him, the indescribable monstrosity hot on your heels. Randolph wrenches open your hand, grabs the key you found in the unnamed house, and clutches it tightly. He closes his eyes and whispers something inaudible. As the abominable torrent crashes into you, everything goes black.

When you awaken, you lie on a flat stone platform overlooking a steep, straight staircase that descends into unknown depths. Behind you, the stairway curls upward into a stone spire that ascends into a hazy mist. In both directions, the entirety of the cavern is dimly lit with grey phosphorescence. Randolph pulls you to your feet. “That was a close one,” he admits. “I never wish to take a journey like that again.” You ask where you are, and he bites his lip, looking out over the bleak, desolate scenery.

“This is the lower plane of the Dreamlands, known as the Underworld. It is an inhospitable place. Many of the creatures we have seen crossing over into our world come from this region. Perhaps our key knew this was our true destination. I think...I think it is gone now,” your guide explains.

You are thunderstruck. Randolph grits his teeth at your reaction and looks away in shame. “Forget it. We no longer need it anyway. Let’s go.” His curt reply echoes off the stone steps. With Randolph leading the way, you continue your descent anew. The Underworld may or may not be where your companions are, but if the creatures invading the world of the waking are indeed from this place, then perhaps here you can find answers.

Resolution 4: In the debris, you spot it: something glinting within the maelstrom of ice-cold air and dust, something that calls to you, whispers your name. You barely hear Randolph shouting as the indescribable monstrosity crashes into him. Despite all odds, you somehow reach the rubble that was once the attic of the house with no name. You realize now what that elusive glimmer was: the polished reflection of a bright silver key. “Use it!” Randolph screams between cries of agony. The abomination climbs atop his body. “Use it now, while you ca—”

The thing cuts Randolph’s cry short as it envelops his body. You clutch the key tightly in your hand and shudder as you watch a thousand shapes of horror devour Randolph whole. You think of your companions, trapped somewhere in a perilous dream far from home, and the key’s glow intensifies, swallowing you as completely as the creature swallowed Randolph. Everything goes white.

When you awaken, you lie on a flat stone platform overlooking a steep, straight staircase that descends into unknown depths. Behind you, the stairway curls upward into a stone spire that ascends into a hazy mist. In both directions, the entirety of the cavern is dimly lit with grey phosphorescence. You search for the Silver Key, but it has vanished. There is no sign of Randolph Carter.

It is clear you are no longer in the waking world. Perhaps the key transported your physical body into the Dreamlands, as Randolph claimed it could. But this place is nothing like the mystical forests, charming medieval villages, and majestic panoramas of which Virgil Gray wrote in his stories. No, far from it: this cold, bleak gulf eats away your hope and replaces it with a feeling of empty, meaningless dread. You peer once more up the countless steps behind you. It seems you have no choice now but to move on, deeper into this desolate and perilous realm.
